test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: A sum was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 4 years. Had it been put at 5% higher rate, it would have fetched ₹520 more. Find the sum.
solution:
**Given:**

Initial time period = 4 years

Difference in interest rate = 5%

Difference in interest amount = ₹520

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be ₹P.

Interest at the original rate = (P × R × 4) / 100

Interest at the increased rate = (P × (R+5) × 4) / 100

Difference in interest = ₹520

⇒ (P × (R+5) × 4) / 100 - (P × R × 4) / 100 = 520

⇒ (P × 4 × (R + 5 - R)) / 100 = 520

⇒ (P × 4 × 5) / 100 = 520

⇒ (P × 20) / 100 = 520

⇒ P × 0.2 = 520

⇒ P = 520 / 0.2

⇒ P = 2600

**The sum is ₹2,600.**
